newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares lower after Washington summit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares lower after Washington summit.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mildly lower on Thursday in sluggish trading as investors remained indifferent to the results of the Israeli-Arab summit in Washington, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 0.80 percent, or 1.48 points, to 182.93. The Maof 25 index fell 0.52 percent to 193.02.
Closing volume was not available because trading of shares in the Karam index of small cap stocks had not finished.
The Tel Aviv bourse closed two hours early throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth. Normal trading hours will resume on October 6.

"The market is in a waiting pattern and was unaffected by the summit's results. Nobody expected that in two days the deep political divisions between Israelis and Palestinans would disappear," said Zvi Hoffman at Meitav Investments.

The two-day summit convened by U.S. President Bill Clinton achieved no concrete results. The summit was an attempt to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palestinians following bloody clashes last week that killed 73 people.
"The market is waiting for political developments and investors want to see the results of the talks next week," Hoffman said.
Israelis and Palestinans agreed to talks starting on Sunday with mediation efforts by U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross.
"Trading was mixed and there was no clear reaction to the Middle East summit. Investors prefer to wait and see if there will be any political developments," said one trader.
"Trading was dull because of the holiday and people want to see how foreign investors will react to the summit's results," she added.

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.75 percent to 140,379 on turnover of 5.0 million shekels; Koor Industries, which lost 0.25 percent to 28,167 on turnover of 3.5 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which fell 2.25 percent to 748 on volume of 2.2 million shekels.
